body:
The current PXD057588 macrophage processing comparison failed to beat a condition-only control. A training-only calibration/capacity diagnostic then produced nonconstant predictions that overfit. We need an independent APC population with explicit machinery perturbation, rather than more feature tuning on the inspected cohort.

Please admit **de Verteuil et al. 2010, PMID 20484733 / PMC2938112 / DOI 10.1074/mcp.M900566-MCP200** through the canonical source/query/recipe system. This is a focused quantitative follow-up to broad mouse-curation issue #13.

Primary source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2938112/ and https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/20484733/ . The indexed primary article describes primary mouse dendritic cells, WT versus LMP7/MECL1 double loss, beta2m-deficient negative controls, three biological replicates per group and 417 identified WT MHC-I peptides (supplemental Table S1). It also reports altered transcripts and reduced LMP2 protein, so the perturbation cannot be represented as an isolated change in one cleavage parameter. These facts motivate admission; source files and table schemas are **not yet independently admitted**.

Required shared contract:

- Retrieve and hash original supplementary assets and any available raw/processed quantitative deposits; retain license/access status and missing assets. Replay source cells and identifiers before declaring readiness.
- Preserve peptide sequences, modifications, parent IDs and all exact candidate origins; original search-reference version; source confidence/FDR/manual-verification statements; per-replicate intensities/ratios/qualifiers and their units/scales. Keep absence, zero, detection limit and unquantified observations distinct. Never convert a WT-only detection into a numeric KO zero.
- Preserve WT/double-loss/beta2m-control roles, measured-cell versus source-protein species, mouse background, DC differentiation/maturation state, biological versus technical replicates, run/fraction membership, contrasts and control contributors. Unknown sample links stay unknown.
- Encode LMP7/MECL1 loss as source-supported concurrent machinery assertions with gene aliases; keep observed LMP2 reduction separate from genotype and unknown catalytic activity. The beta2m condition is a specificity/background control, not an ordinary peptide-abundance training negative. Do not infer unreported loss of other processing components.
- Keep MHC class and sample allele repertoire distinct from algorithmically assigned peptide restriction. Retain the assignment method, alternatives and nonclassical-MHC status. Predicted allele assignments are not measured single-allele labels.
- Preserve transcript measurements as RNA evidence, not measured protein precursor abundance. Capture any available protein-level evidence and its exact pairing precision separately. Do not assume input abundance is unchanged by the genotype.
- Make source metadata, assay channels, contrasts/derivation inputs, context assertions, parent mappings and training eligibility accessible through the existing EvidenceStore/row-recipe API. Retain all source rows and explicit dispositions; no Presto-specific workbook parser.

Admission gates: original-value replay; full contributor lineage; no unit/qualifier coercion; all source-dependent rows grouped before filtering; documented repeat/sample/reference ambiguity; an explicit quantitative recipe that excludes unsupported quantities without erasing their source records. Freeze any future evaluation split before fitting. This is MHC-eluted response evidence, **not a direct label of free intracellular concentrations**, and it does not by itself identify processing independently of selection or observation.

Repository check: the inspected Hitlist checkout b3f1079 has generic immunoproteasome vocabulary but no explicit adapter/reference for this PMID; exact PMID/DOI issue searches returned no result. The broad #13 covers mouse data generally. If another canonical route already admits the complete quantitative source, link it and reuse it rather than duplicate it.
title: Admit quantitative dendritic-cell immunoproteasome-loss source (PMID 20484733) with complete context
